title: Twenty nations ask the UN to police AI, US and China disagree
description:
Twenty nations and the EU asked the UN for an AI watchdog to oversee compliance while the US and OpenAI pushed a rival US-led rulebook, Anthropic shipped Claude Opus 5.5 at 40% lower cost and OpenAI released GPT-6 Sol and Luna the same day at half price, and Pew found the share of Americans calling data centers bad for the environment jumped from 39% to 54% as $68 billion in projects stalled.

https://sharedsapience.com/the-century-report-september-23-2026/

0:00 Open and framing
0:34 Twenty nations ask the UN to referee AI
4:20 Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 land the same day
7:10 Data-center opinion turns sharply
10:29 CAIRN finds autonomous AI malware
13:26 Rat-neuron video model reaches AWS
15:53 AI reads cancer from chest CT scans
17:43 Close

This episode covers the UN AI-watchdog coalition and OpenAI's US-led counterproposal, the Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 same-day price war, the sharp turn in data-center public opinion and the EU's disclosure rules, Cisco Talos's CAIRN framework and the autonomous CLOSEDQUORUM malware, The Biological Computing Company's rat-neuron video model on AWS, and an AI reading esophageal cancer from ordinary chest CT scans.

Get the written edition free, every day: https://sharedsapience.com/century-report/?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=description&utm_campaign=tcr-daily

On September 21, twenty countries and the European Union asked the UN to stand up a body to set standards, oversee compliance, and convene states once AI systems cross defined capability thresholds - a coalition that includes Germany, Kenya, and Kazakhstan but leaves out the US, China, and the UK. OpenAI answered with a narrower US-led club on the argument that the labs at the frontier should hold the pen, and Trump rejected international oversight as a "globalist scheme." The same week, Anthropic shipped Opus 5.5 at Fable-level performance for 40% less and OpenAI released GPT-6 Sol and Luna the same day at roughly half price, driving the frontier into a comparison-shopping phase. Pew found data-center opposition climbing to 54% as the EU proposed efficiency-disclosure rules. Cisco Talos released an open framework that surfaced malware taking direction from four AI models at once, Microsoft dismantled a crime service that had compromised 12,000 accounts, a rat-neuron-tuned video model reached AWS, and an AI read esophageal cancer from ordinary chest CT scans at 90% sensitivity across more than 80,000 patients.
